title: The Sixteenth Group Chat
premise: Ada Montrose, a scholarship student at Hollowmere Academy, has survived three years by staying invisible—until her history teacher pairs her with Theo Vance, the golden boy whose family built the town, for a project on the academy's founding. Digging into archives, they uncover the Sixteenth Group Chat: a secret society of six students who, generations ago, made a bargain that keeps Hollowmere funded and its founders' crimes buried, renewed every fifty years by a ritual that now demands a scapegoat—and this year's is Ada. As the town closes ranks and the deadline approaches, Ada and Theo must decide whether to destroy the tradition that made Hollowmere or inherit it; in the end they expose the founding crime publicly, shattering the bargain at the cost of Theo's family name and Ada's scholarship, but winning something rarer than survival: a town forced to face its own inheritance.
about_author: C. M. Ravensworth is a former boarding school archivist who spent years cataloguing letters no one was supposed to read. They write young adult fiction about institutions, secrets, and the teenagers stubborn enough to burn them down.

chapters.title: Fine
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A day in Ada's carefully managed invisibility at Hollowmere Academy: perfect grades, perfect silence, a scholarship she guards like a wound. When her name appears on the semester project pairing list beside Theo Vance—the boy whose family owns half the town—her stomach drops. Beat: dread disguised as composure.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo resents being paired with the scholarship girl who once humiliated him in debate class, but Mr. Okafor insists their topic is 'the founding of Hollowmere.' In the archive basement, their first argument cracks into uneasy truce over a locked cabinet neither of them can explain. Beat: friction sparking curiosity.

chapters.title: Sixteen Names
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Behind the cabinet they find a ledger listing fifteen 'group chats'—student cohorts across 150 years—and a sixteenth entry sealed with wax, dated to renew this spring. The last renewal coincided with a student's quiet expulsion and disappearance. Beat: first chill of real stakes.

chapters.title: Deniability
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo asks his grandmother about the Sixteenth Group Chat and watches her smile die mid-sentence. She warns him off with a story about a cousin who 'asked too many questions.' He lies to Ada about what he learned, then can't sleep. Beat: loyalty beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: The Scapegoat Clause
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Decoding the ledger's margins, they find the bargain's terms: Hollowmere's endowment survives only if each generation offers up one outsider to carry the founders' guilt—a student blamed, expelled, erased. Every name matches an 'incident' in school lore. The sixteenth slot is blank. Beat: horror clicking into place.

chapters.title: Everyone Already Knows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They test the water: classmates deflect, teachers change subjects, the headmaster offers Ada a mysterious 'hardship grant.' The whole town is a conspiracy of politeness. Ada realizes her invisibility wasn't luck—it was management. Beat: paranoia blooming.

chapters.title: What Theo Inherits
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the Vance estate, Theo finds his grandfather's copy of the ledger with annotations naming him as the intended sixteenth 'keeper'—the one who administers the choice. His family expects him to pick the scapegoat. Everyone assumes he'll pick Ada. Beat: the trap of legacy.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada confronts Theo; instead of betrayal, he burns his annotated copy and proposes they break the tradition together. They recruit Priya, the archivist's granddaughter, who reveals the disappeared students didn't all leave—one stayed, hidden, watching. Beat: alliance forged from enemies.

chapters.title: The One Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Following decades-old maintenance records, they find Ruth Ellery, the fifteenth scapegoat, living under a false name as the school's night custodian. Ruth tells them the truth: the bargain isn't supernatural—it's money, blackmail, and a board of trustees who will do anything to keep it. Beat: myth deflating into something scarier.

chapters.title: Paper Trails
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ruth hands over her evidence: letters proving the founder's fortune came from stolen land and a covered-up death. But exposing it means destroying the endowment—Ada's scholarship, Priya's mother's job, everyone's futures. Ada hesitates for the first time. Beat: the price becomes personal.

chapters.title: Spring Formal, Spring Trap
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The trustees move early: Theo is caught with archive keys he didn't take, and the school announces his suspension. It's a message—they can frame anyone. Ada realizes the blank sixteenth slot was never going to be filled by ritual. It gets filled by whoever asks questions. Beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Records begin changing: Ada's grades flagged, her scholarship 'under review,' her debate victory scrubbed from the website. Ruth warns them the board did this before, to her, in eleven days flat. Time is already running out. Beat: gaslighting made institutional.

chapters.title: The Fifteenth's Mistake
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth confesses why she stayed silent for fifty years: she tried to fight alone, and the board destroyed not just her but the friend who helped her. She begs Ada not to repeat it—but gives her the one thing she never had: allies, and a plan. Beat: mentorship through regret.

chapters.title: Divide the Town
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The trio goes local: shopkeepers whose families lost land, alumni with old grudges, a journalist expelled in 1989. The town's memory is longer than the academy assumed. Slowly, witnesses agree to talk—if someone goes first. Beat: hope built from ordinary courage.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The headmaster offers Ada everything: full ride, Ivy recommendation, her record cleaned—if she returns the ledger and names her accomplices. For one long scene, alone in his office, she almost says yes. Survival has always been her religion. Beat: temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ada tells Theo she refused, and why: 'Invisible people don't get to choose. I want to choose.' Theo, in turn, chooses publicly—he walks into assembly and resigns his family's seat on the board. His grandmother disowns him by text. Beat: both leads burning their exits.

chapters.title: Founders' Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The board schedules the renewal ceremony inside Founders' Day, planning to expel Ada onstage behind pageantry. The trio's counterplan: during the ceremony, the town's witnesses will read the founder's letters aloud, one by one, from the crowd. Everything depends on timing and nerve. Beat: calm before detonation.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Mid-ceremony, the first witness stands. Then another. The headmaster cuts the microphones; Priya's livestream doesn't care. The letters land like blows—stolen land, a dead boy, fifty years of purchased silence. The crowd turns. Beat: catharsis, public and irreversible.

chapters.title: What the Board Does Next
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Cornered, the board tries one last erasure—calling police on the students, claiming theft of archives. But Ruth steps forward with her own name and testimony, and the officers, locals themselves, hesitate. The law outside the law: a town deciding, together, whom it believes. Beat: power shifting hands.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the emptied archive, Ada and Theo burn the ledger—not to hide the past, but to end the mechanism that traded students for solvency. Ada loses her scholarship; Theo loses his name. Standing in the smoke, they realize they're free and unmoored in equal measure. Beat: grief and liberation entwined.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Weeks later: trustees resign, the endowment restructures under court oversight, Ruth Ellery's expulsion is formally reversed. The school survives, diminished and honest. Priya archives the scandal openly—no more locked cabinets. Beat: justice as slow, unglamorous repair.

chapters.title: The Seventeenth Group Chat
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, final chapter. On the last day of term, Ada, Theo, and Priya start a group chat named 'Seventeen'—not a secret society, but a standing promise to watch the watchers. Ada, no longer invisible, writes the first message: 'We're fine. Actually fine, this time.' Beat: inheritance reclaimed as vigilance, ending on earned hope.
